[1] SpaceXAI recently launched the Grok Bot and Grok 4.6 models with assistance from Cursor.

[2] Update (August 14, 2026): SpaceXAI has completed its acquisition of Cursor.

[3] Update (June 16, 2026): SpaceX acquired Cursor a week after going public.

[4] The original article has been updated as follows:

[5] SpaceX's $10 Billion Deal with Cursor Preceded a $60 Billion Acquisition

[6] Cursor has long been a favorite among software engineers who use Macs to write code with AI. It was among the first services to integrate large language model AI into the application development workflow.

[7] In April, SpaceX and Cursor said the two companies were "working closely together to build the world's leading AI for coding and knowledge work."

[8] The original partnership agreement included SpaceX paying Cursor $1 billion:

[9] In April — before the acquisition — Cursor disclosed further details of the partnership:

[10] Cursor is working with SpaceX to accelerate our model training efforts. Composer, first released six months ago, was our first agentic coding model. Since then, Composer 1.5 scaled reinforcement learning by more than 20x. Composer 2 added continual pre-training to achieve frontier-level performance at a fraction of the cost of other models. With each layer of increased scale, model capabilities grow dramatically. We have long wanted to push our training efforts to the next level, but have been constrained by compute. Through this partnership, our team will leverage xAI's Colossus infrastructure to significantly advance our models' intelligence.

[11] The SpaceX and Cursor partnership further strengthens a competitor to Anthropic's Claude Code and OpenAI Codex agentic coding software.
